steps.what: Read the existing classroom inventory and actual material or equipment requests
Check physical classroom equipment and supplies, count stock and determine suitable items for the actual distribution
Distribute the checked classroom equipment and supplies to the actual intended classroom users
Update the existing classroom inventory with observed stock and actual equipment distribution
Save the updated classroom inventory in its existing working file

tasks.design: Use the existing classroom inventory in {DOCS} or the school's equipment register {OTHER}, with native item views and an update form. Counting, condition checks, choosing suitable items and physical distribution remain human; the record is updated only from actual observations and completed distribution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing inventory references and repeated item headings can require unnecessary navigation and copying.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item views and forms can reuse those headings without sensing stock or moving items.
tasks.still_hard: Actual quantity, condition, accessibility and appropriate use require physical checks and teacher judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher knows whether a particular aid is suitable and safe for the child and activity.

ambition.what: The same classroom stock is controlled with less repeated reference work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing inventory views and forms can reduce navigation and repeated item fields, but physical counts and classroom distribution remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary covers an actual classroom inventory/distribution episode and the inventory already used to locate and replenish items. Do not invent a separate custody log or distribution report where none is kept.

{OTHER} means the school's existing equipment register and physical classroom aids. The existing register owner supplies item ID/description, location and prior quantity where actually recorded. s1 counts real source reading; s2 produces actual count, condition and suitable-item decision, and s4 retains manual update capture. No sensors or free stock dataset are assumed.

Test the native item view/form first. s1 removes 3 of 15 navigation units and retains 12 reading units. s4 removes 1.8 of 9 units of repeated item headings and field navigation, retaining 7.2 for actual counts, locations and checks. Physical work retains all its time; these are unmeasured estimates.

a1 is the teacher's real current suitability decision for the exact items and users, made during s2's physical condition check. It is an operational gate on actual distribution, not an added supervisory review or an approval of the teacher's note. Changed condition, item, user or activity voids it.

s5 is ordinary same-system persistence at the minimum share, fully retained and ungated with no gain. Incremental work includes form/reference repair beyond retained count and record checks. No new purchasing order or external send is assumed.
unknowns: Actual classroom inventory use and native fields
research_questions: Observe the existing stock check, actual distribution and record update separately.
Test a damaged aid and changed intended user without carrying forward stale suitability.

already_counted.description: Inventory reading, all physical counts/condition checks and distribution, actual update capture and persistence remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Maintain item references and form fields and repair broken links beyond retained physical and record checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact items, current physical condition, intended users and activity checked in s2; any change voids the operational distribution decision.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=12+35+40+7.2+1=95.2. Gross 4.8 less 1 upkeep gives net 3.8. Conservative case: unindexed legacy items retain 14.5 of 15 lookup units and irregular item descriptions retain 8.5 of 9 update units. One gross unit just covers upkeep; physical work is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the actual learning objectives and pupil access needs for the experiential activity
Plan and write the actual class-project or demonstration sequence, roles, materials and access arrangements
Coordinate actual classroom support roles and practical activity arrangements with the staff involved
Prepare the actual experiential activity space and physical materials
outputs: prepared accessible activity space and materials

steps.what: Supervise the experiential learning activity and adapt it to actual pupil participation and needs
inputs: prepared accessible activity space and materials

tasks.design: Use existing objective links in {LMS} and the current activity template in {DOCS} for a classroom project or demonstration. Retain activity design, staff coordination, physical preparation with classroom aids {OTHER} and live supervision; the template only reuses repeated requirements and layout fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Classroom activity plans repeat objective references, roles and material headings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing links and planning fields can reuse those references without designing or supervising the activity.
tasks.still_hard: Access, actual participation, behaviour and the practical activity require direct teacher judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher keeps the experience meaningful and responds to children's needs in real time.

ambition.what: The same experiential activity remains teacher-designed and supervised.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: objective links and activity templates can reduce repeated planning fields, while experiential learning design and supervision remain human.

assumptions: The representative episode is a classroom project or demonstration, both explicitly within the task. It includes the actual activity plan used by the teacher and staff, not an invented post-activity report. Field trips and guest visits may additionally require bookings, parent notices and formal school approval; those actual writing, final-version approval and send/commit steps must be added before pricing those variants.

The teacher's existing curriculum/support records supply objective reference, access needs and version; s1 counts reading and any manual source fallback. s2 produces actual activity sequence, roles and materials with all professional design and suitability checks retained. s3 produces real staff arrangements, not a free availability feed.

Test native objective links and the existing activity template first. s1 removes 2 of 10 units of repeated objective navigation. s2 removes 3 of 15 units of repeated objective, role and material-header entry and layout; the remaining 12 units retain actual design, writing and checking. These are separately sized unmeasured work estimates.

Ordinary working persistence is included in s2 at near-zero fully retained time, without approval or saving. s3 is a live internal planning conversation, not a hidden written notice or external booking. Physical preparation and supervision retain their full shares.
{OTHER} means physical classroom activity aids. No model, pupil scoring, recording or new report is needed. Link and template repair beyond actual planning checks is counted below.
unknowns: Actual activity type and existing plan use
Additional actual authority and send steps for trips or guests
research_questions: Observe a classroom activity from real planning to supervised participation.
For any trip or guest variant, map its real booking, final-version release and notification actions before extending the estimate.

already_counted.description: Actual requirements reading, activity design/checking, staff conversation, physical preparation and supervision remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Maintain objective links and activity template fields and repair broken references beyond retained planning checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=8+12+10+10+55=95. Gross 5 less 1 upkeep gives net 4. Conservative case: a new activity uses unlinked objectives and a bespoke sequence, retaining all 10 lookup units and 14 of 15 plan units. One gross unit only covers upkeep; physical preparation, staff coordination and supervision remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical classroom work and professional judgement remain central; existing reference views and planning fields offer small reductions in repeated record work.
skills_to_grow: Tie inventory updates to actual counts and distribution
Check activity accessibility and real staff responsibilities
Identify the actual release actions needed for off-site activities
role.ambitious_version: Keep classroom materials and experiential activities usable and well supported, without adding administrative records merely to automate them.
